question: Which statement best describes Request Memoization?
options: In the browser, Next keeps an in-memory cache of visited route segments' RSC payloads so back/forward and link navigations feel instant without refetching. It's per-session and time-limited; `router.refresh()` or a server revalidation clears the relevant entries.

Within a single render pass, Next dedupes identical `fetch` calls (same URL + options) so calling the same fetch in a layout and a page hits the network once. It's React-level, per-request, and clears when the render finishes — purely an optimization so you can fetch where you need data without prop-drilling.

At build time (and on revalidation) Next caches the rendered HTML and RSC payload of statically-rendered routes. Serving from it is the fastest path. A route opts out (becomes dynamic) if it uses dynamic functions (cookies/headers/searchParams) or uncached data.

A persistent, server-side cache of `fetch` results that survives across requests and deployments. By default cacheable fetches are stored here; you control it with `next: { revalidate }` (time-based) and `next: { tags }` (on-demand). This is what makes SSG/ISR possible.

question: Which statement best describes Data Cache?
options: A persistent, server-side cache of `fetch` results that survives across requests and deployments. By default cacheable fetches are stored here; you control it with `next: { revalidate }` (time-based) and `next: { tags }` (on-demand). This is what makes SSG/ISR possible.

In the browser, Next keeps an in-memory cache of visited route segments' RSC payloads so back/forward and link navigations feel instant without refetching. It's per-session and time-limited; `router.refresh()` or a server revalidation clears the relevant entries.

The Data Cache is driven by fetch options: omit options to cache indefinitely, add `revalidate: N` for time-based ISR, and add `tags: ['x']` so you can purge that exact data later with `revalidateTag('x')`. Tags are the most precise invalidation tool.

question: Which statement best describes Router Cache (client)?
options: After a mutation, call `revalidatePath('/blog')` to purge a route's cached data/HTML, or `revalidateTag('posts')` to purge every fetch tagged `posts`. This refreshes the Data Cache and Full Route Cache so the next request rebuilds with fresh data — the backbone of on-demand ISR.

Read top-down by lifetime: Request Memoization (this render) → Data Cache (across requests, server) → Full Route Cache (rendered output, server/CDN) → Router Cache (this browser session). Bugs usually come from forgetting one layer is still serving old data after a change.
